words.gloss: the act of concealing or hiding wealth
those who do not have (the evil of concealing)

literal: If one sees those who do not have the evil of concealing wealth, all the affliction of poverty will perish at once.
translation: If those who ask meet people who are free from the mean habit of hiding their wealth, all the misery of their poverty will vanish at once.
modern: தம்மிடம் உள்ளதை மறைத்து வைக்கும் தீய குணம் இல்லாதவர்களைக் கண்டால், வறுமையினால் உண்டாகும் துன்பங்கள் அனைத்தும் உடனே நீங்கிவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the profound relief a needy person feels upon encountering a truly generous giver. The word 'karappu' refers to the act of hiding or withholding one's wealth when someone asks for help, which is described here as an 'iṭumpai' (an evil or painful trait). When a seeker finds someone free from this withholding nature ('karappiṭumpai illārai'), their own 'nirappiṭumpai' (the misery of poverty) instantly disappears. The mere sight of such a noble person brings immediate comfort, as the seeker knows their distress is already resolved.
